chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, hates al-qil wa al-qal (idle talk/gossip), wastage of wealth, and abundant questioning.'

key_terms.الْقِيلَ وَ الْقَالَ: Idle talk or gossip; literally 'it was said' and 'he said', referring to trivial or backbiting conversation

ai.seo_question: What are the three things Allah hates according to this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies three specific vices that incur Allah's displeasure: al-qil wa al-qal (idle talk or gossip), israf (wasteful expenditure), and excessive questioning (kathrat al-su'al). This triad highlights the spiritual dangers of verbal frivolity, financial negligence, and intellectual curiosity that leads to distraction or doubt, offering a concise guide for personal conduct in Shia ethical tradition.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Hates ‘الْقِيلَ وَ الْقَالَ’ (the ‘It was said such’, and ‘he said such’, i.e., useless discussions and arguments), and wastage of the wealth, and abundant questioning’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Asbat from certain persons of our people from ‘Amr ibn abu al-Miqdam who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
One’s trusting a treacherous person and wasting assets is a worthless act.’”
